title: Om: three sounds and a silence
hookLine: Death gives a boy one word, and two schools hear its silence differently
carry: om holds waking, dream, sleep, and the silent self
tomorrow: why does an Upanishad stop to talk about honey?

lines: THE WORD ALL THE VEDAS POINT TO: OM.
cards: A boy waits three nights at Death's door, and Death, who kept a guest waiting, owes him three wishes. In the Katha Upanishad, Nachiketa spends the last one asking what happens to a person after death.

Somewhere in his answer, Yama, the lord of death, gives him one word: the word all the Vedas point to, he says, is Om. The Mandukya Upanishad takes that syllable apart: ah, oo, mmm, then a beat of silence.
It calls the silence the fourth part, the heart of it all. Two great schools of Vedanta agree on that much. They don't agree on what lives in the silence.

teach.h: A, U, M: WAKING, DREAM, SLEEP.
teach.b: First, the text. The Mandukya lays this self over Om. A is waking, the self that deals with the world outside.
U is dreaming, at home in an inner world. M is deep sleep, where everything gathers into one.
And the fourth has no sound part at all. It is peaceful, kind, not two.
That, the text says, is the self. Now the two readings. Advaita teachers read the Mandukya through verses tradition credits to Gaudapada, and through Shankara.
For them, the fourth is the one self that was there all along. Waking, dream and sleep pass across it like weather across the sky, and not two means just that: there is no second thing.

teach.h: MADHVA: THE LORD, BEYOND ALL THREE.
teach.b: Madhva's school reads the same Upanishad and hears the Lord in it. The quarters, it says, name forms of Vishnu, who is present in waking, dream and sleep and stands beyond them all.
The self who knows him is real, depends on him, and never becomes him. Both schools take the Mandukya as scripture. Both chant the same Om.
One hears the silence as the self with nothing beside it; the other hears the Lord holding everything that is.
And this is why Hindus begin and end prayer, study, even a wedding card, with Om: in this teaching, one syllable holds every state you'll ever be in, and the quiet beneath them all.

how: Om is chanted at the start and end of prayers and study; students of the Mandukya chant it slowly and rest in the silence after it, and teachers of different Vedanta schools explain that silence in their own ways.

o: a chant said only at funerals and endings
a word for the breath held between two prayers
this self is Brahman, heard in Om's sounds and silence

games.q: Om, quarter by quarter. tap the pairs.
p: deep sleep: all gathered into one
no sound: peaceful, kind, not two

s: the silence after Om is just a pause between chants
the Mandukya calls the soundless fourth peaceful, kind, not two: the self.
every Hindu school reads the Mandukya's fourth the same way
Advaita and Madhva's school read it differently, and both take the Mandukya as scripture.
in the Mandukya, A, U and M stand for waking, dream and deep sleep
and the fourth has no sound part at all.

games.q: you lean toward the Advaita reading. a friend from a Madhva family says the silent fourth points to the Lord. state her side's best case.
o: she's mostly being loyal to how her family was raised.
the quarters name forms of Vishnu, present in all three states and beyond them.
her school doesn't count the Mandukya as scripture, so it can't really say.
games.why: Madhva's school reads the Mandukya's quarters as forms of Vishnu, who is in waking, dream and sleep and beyond them; the knowing self is real and depends on him.

practice: If you're somewhere you can, say Om once, slowly, out loud: ah, oo, mmm. Then stay in the silence after it for a few breaths before the next one. Keep going at your own pace, listening as closely to the quiet as to the sound.

wordCard.voice: Ayam atma brahma, through the Mandukya: Om's three sounds as waking, dream and sleep, and a fourth that makes no sound, peaceful, kind, not two.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the sacred syllable, which the Mandukya hears as A, U, M and a silence.

carryVoice: Something to keep: Om holds waking, dream and sleep, and the silence after it is the self. Two schools hear that silence in their own ways. Until tomorrow.
